title: Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards Payments Training Questions: Returned-Payment Add-Back
content:
**What is the returned-payment add-back on a catch-up payment?** On a Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards account, the returned-payment add-back is set by what became of the most recent payment credited after the missed due date (the payment due date of the statement of the billing period the most recent late fee belongs to): when it was returned unpaid and a returned payment fee was assessed for it, the add-back is the returned amount plus that fee; when it was returned unpaid with no such fee, the add-back is the returned amount; otherwise there is no add-back.

**Where does it enter?** The returned-payment add-back is added into the catch-up amount before the most recent payment credited after the missed due date is subtracted, the floor at zero applied and the result rounded.

**Which records show it?** A returned-payment entry pointing to that payment, and a fee entry of the returned payment fee type pointing to the same payment.

## Cases (hypothetical: USD 55.00 owed before the add-back; most recent payment USD 60.00 credited after the missed due date)

| What became of the USD 60.00 payment | Add-back | Catch-up amount |
|---|---|---|
| returned unpaid; USD 29.00 returned payment fee assessed for it | USD 89.00 | 55.00 plus 89.00 less 60.00: USD 84.00 |
| returned unpaid; no fee assessed for it | USD 60.00 | 55.00 plus 60.00 less 60.00: USD 55.00 |
| not returned | none | 55.00 less 60.00, floored: zero |
